notes.title: Developer's Notes #2: End of the Closed Beta Part 2
notes.content:
[p]Hello, this is the [i]Chrono Odyssey[/i] Development Team.[/p][p][/p][p]As a continuation of [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2873440/view/532102384016429258"]Part 1[/url], this follow-up developer note will cover additional areas we’re actively working to improve. What we’ll be addressing are:[/p][list][*][p][b]Combat Systems (2/2)[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Content & Open World[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Progression & Gameplay Flexibility[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Technical Stability[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Art (Design & Animations)[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]UI & UX[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Balance[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Social Features[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]In-game Guidance[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Sound[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Narrative[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]Before we dive into the details, we’d like to once again thank everyone who joined the recent closed beta and took the time to share their feedback.[/p][p]
As always, your insights and suggestions are deeply appreciated, as they play a pivotal role in refining [i]Chrono Odyssey[/i] and shaping the journey ahead.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44935330/edefb80aad09830f171afe3a641ac60954e224e5.jpg"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][olist][*][p]Controls[/p][/*][*][p]Hit Feedback[/p][/*][*][p]Damage Feedback[/p][/*][*][p]Skill[/p][/*][*][p]Class[/p][/*][*][p]Weapon Swap[/p][/*][*][p]Balance[/p][/*][*][p]Camera & FOV[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy AI[/p][/*][*][p]Difficulty[/p][/*][*][p]PvP[/p][/*][/olist][p][/p][h2][b]1. Controls[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Input Responsiveness[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Long recovery frames made it difficult to input new commands during ongoing animations.[/p][/*][*][p]Certain motions remained unresponsive even after visual completion.[/p][/*][*][p]Weapon swapping and other combat actions suffered from input buffering, resulting in delayed response.[/p][/*][*][p]Some content felt sluggish due to latency issues.[/p][/*][*][p]UI interactions lacked clear visual feedback, making it hard to confirm whether an input was registered.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]We’ll be adjusting the interruption timing for movement, attack, and skill animations to improve responsiveness.[/p][/*][*][p]The buffering window for inputs will be significantly reduced to prevent unintended actions from being triggered.[/p][/*][*][p]Colors and effects across all interactions will be adjusted, and a unified UI kit will be introduced to improve clarity and visual feedback.[/p][/*][*][p]A system-level feedback cue will be added when players attempt to cancel out a non-interruptible action.[/p][/*][*][p]To further improve input responsiveness, we’ll be reviewing client-server packet transmission and optimizing network performance.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]B. [u]Controller / Keyboard & Mouse Experience[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]The current UI was not specifically designed with either control scheme in mind, resulting in inconsistent and uncomfortable experiences across both setups.[/p][/*][*][p]Many in-game interactions were developed around controller input, making keyboard & mouse controls feel unintuitive.[/p][p]Controller users experienced difficulties with ranged targeting, and lacked access to fine-tuned settings such sensitivity adjustment, vibration/haptic feedback, accessibility options, and overall responsiveness.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Keyboard & Mouse[/b][/p][list][*][p]UX will be optimized specifically for keyboard & mouse environments.[/p][/*][*][p]Hold interactions, which are commonly used for controller inputs, will be minimized or removed.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Controller[/b][/p][list][*][p]UX will be optimized specifically for controller environments.[/p][/*][*][p]UI pages with inconvenient key mapping (e.g., Inventory) will be redesigned for better navigation.[/p][/*][*][p]Preset options inspired by Soulslike and MMORPG control schemes will also be added.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Universal Improvements[/b][/p][list][*][p]UI navigation depth will be minimized, and essential functions will be reassigned to more accessible buttons.[/p][/*][*][p]To support more personalized control experiences, custom key mapping options and various input settings such as sensitivity scaling and input inversion will be enhanced.[/p][/*][*][p]We’ll be improving the lock-on feature to reduce control inconsistencies during combat for a more seamless experience.[/p][/*][*][p]Skills will now consistently target locked-on enemies, rather than firing based on the current camera direction.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][/p][h2][b]2. Hit Feedback[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Hit Feedback[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Monsters had excessively high stagger thresholds, resulting in weak hit reactions and reduced sense of impact.[/p][/*][*][p] Crowd control effects had extremely short durations, making it difficult to take advantage of said effects during combat.[/p][/*][*][p]It was often hard to measure the correct distance needed to land attacks.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Hit reactions will occur more frequently, and knockback effects will be added to make hits easier to recognize.[/p][list][*][p]Enemy attack patterns will be adjusted to allow for varied player responses such as parrying, countering, blocking, and dodging, adding more depth to combat.[/p][/*][*][p]The same reactive effects will be applied to enemy attacks, enhancing the sense of impact and increasing combat tension.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]All enemy hit reactions will be reviewed to identify missing animations, which will be implemented as needed.[/p][/*][*][p]Hit reaction behaviors will be standardized across monster types to support experience-based learning and improve clarity in encounters.[/p][/*][*][p]Damage floaters and HP bar animations will be enhanced to make successful hits more noticeable.[/p][/*][*][p]CC durations will be increased to 2-4 seconds, making successful crowd control effects more apparent and allowing more opportunities for follow-up attacks.[/p][p] [/p][/*][/list][h2][b]3. Damage Feedback[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Damage Feedback[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Damage feedback often felt weak, reducing the sense of impact when taking hits.[/p][/*][*][p]Incoming damage often went unnoticed when players were interacting with menus.[/p][/*][*][p]Misaligned hitboxes and network latency caused outcomes that didn’t match what was displayed on screen.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Damage notifications will be improved to ensure players recognize incoming damage, even while using the in-game menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy attack motions, visual effects, and hitboxes will be aligned to improve clarity.[/p][/*][*][p]Client-server response times will be optimized to minimize hit and damage timing delays.[/p][/*][*][p]New hit reaction animations will be added based on the type of enemy attack, improving the visibility of effects like stagger and knockback.[/p][/*][*][p] Sound and camera effects will be enhanced to improve the sense of impact.[/p][/*][*][p]Baseline hit animations will be refined so that attacks produce a consistent and noticeable visual reaction.[/p][p] [/p][/*][/list][h2][b]4. Skill[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Skill Synergies[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Skill chaining felt difficult to execute due to lack of synergy between abilities.[/p][/*][*][p]Passive skill enhancements were often more efficient, reducing incentive to use active skill combos.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]The skill system will be refined to support a wider range of playstyles, even within the same class or weapon.[/p][/*][*][p]Each weapon will support four distinct combat styles, allowing players to create builds based on their progression path.[/p][/*][*][p]Skill synergies will not be limited to a single weapon. Skills across different weapons will link together, opening up various combinations.[/p][/*][*][p]We will continue to develop skill chaining and progression systems over time, reinforcing a structure that’s easy to grasp yet hard to master.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]B. [u]Skill Descriptions & Indicators[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Some skill descriptions were too long and hard to understand.[/p][/*][*][p]It was unclear which effects corresponded to each buff icon.[/p][/*][*][p] Buffs and debuffs had visibility issues, and it was hard to track their duration.[/p][/*][*][p]The Chronotector's Summon ability lacked in-game guidance.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Skill descriptions will be refined, with videos added to active skills for better clarity.[/p][/*][*][p]The HUD for buffs and debuffs will be redesigned to improve visibility, with new effects added when buffs or debuffs are applied for better player awareness.[/p][/*][*][p]Summon UI will be updated to display specter types, backstories, abilities, and enhancement details.[/p][p] [/p][/*][/list][h2][b]5. Class[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Class Balance[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]All classes currently share similar roles (tank/healer/DPS), lacking distinct identity.[/p][/*][*][p]Ranged classes are easier to play compared to melee classes.[/p][/*][*][p]Monster AI does not pose a meaningful threat to ranged classes.[/p][/*][*][p]There are significant balance discrepancies between the three weapons available for each class.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Monster AI will be improved to ensure monsters respond more effectively to ranged attacks.[/p][/*][*][p]Introduction of the Matrix system (skill tree nodes)[/p][list][*][p]The Matrix will allow players to choose specific roles for each weapon, reinforcing  combat style identity.[/p][/*][*][p] Even when using the same weapon, players will be able to choose from four distinct styles based on their progression path.[/p][/*][*][p]Based on progression paths, the same skill may deliver a different combat experience.[/p][/*][*][p]With the introduction of the Matrix system, all classes will be re-evaluated for combat balance.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]6. Weapon Swap[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Weapon Swap[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Weapon swaps often felt delayed, occurring only after skill animations ended.[/p][/*][*][p]Pressing the weapon swap key multiple times could queue several inputs, often causing the wrong weapon to be equipped.[/p][/*][*][p]When swapping weapons during combat, it was often difficult to recognize which weapon was currently in use.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Skill recovery times will be reduced to allow smoother weapon swaps during ongoing skill animations.[/p][/*][*][p]The buffer window for weapon swaps will be shortened to less than 1 second so that swaps feel more responsive.[/p][/*][*][p]A short cooldown will be applied to swaps, preventing unintended double swaps.[/p][/*][*][p]HUD design for equipped weapons will be enhanced to improve visibility during combat.[/p][/*][*][p]Visual and HUD effects will be added to make transitions more noticeable.[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h2][b]7. Balance[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Combat Depth & Pacing[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Combat patterns focus too heavily on dodging and attacking, making encounters feel simplistic and repetitive.[/p][/*][*][p]All classes offered a similar combat experience, weakening class identity and variety.[/p][/*][*][p]Lack of proper hit and damage feedback made all encounters feel similar.[/p][/*][*][p]Awkward enemy AI and animations disrupted combat pacing and broke immersion.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Enemy AI will be adjusted to react to player movement, rather than solely following priority-based action sequences.[/p][/*][*][p]Wind-up animations for enemy skills that inflict knockbacks, stuns, and knockdowns will be improved to better signal danger and allow players to respond accordingly.[/p][/*][*][p]The Matrix system will introduce various combat styles, even for players using the same weapon.[/p][/*][*][p]Through the Matrix system, players will be able to create and combine various builds that match their preference.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]B. [u]Enemy Patterns[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Combat difficulty felt unintentionally high due to unclear attack telegraphs, making it difficult to time dodges or attacks.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Monsters with subtle pre-attack motions will have more noticeable animations to make it easier for players to anticipate incoming attacks.[/p][/*][*][p]FOV and sensitivity settings will be improved to give players a clearer view of enemy movement.[/p][/*][*][p]Patterns with wide hitboxes or long tracking sequences will be adjusted, making it easier to dodge or block incoming attacks.[/p][/*][*][p]Players will no longer be instantly defeated by bosses unless they’re significantly underleveled.[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h2][b]8. Camera & FOV[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Camera Movement & Angles[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]The camera zoomed in too close to the character near walls or certain environments, hindering visibility.[/p][/*][*][p]Vertical camera shaking hindered gameplay experience, especially when traversing uneven terrain.[/p][/*][*][p]Locking onto large monsters fixed the camera at an upward angle, limiting visibility during combat.[/p][/*][*][p]In certain situations, the camera tracked too slowly, causing it to fall behind the attack direction.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Objects between the character and camera will turn transparent to maintain clear visibility.[/p][/*][*][p]Camera movement will be smoothed out to reduce excessive screen shaking.[/p][/*][*][p]Lock-on positions will be adjusted based on monster type to ensure camera angles are better suited for combat.[/p][/*][*][p]Attacks and skills will now directly target the locked-on enemy, rather than following the camera’s facing direction.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h2][b]9. Enemy AI[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Enemy AI & Response Time[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Aggro detection and response times were too slow, reducing combat tension and immersion.[/p][/*][*][p]Enemies often failed to react immediately after taking damage or spotting a player.[/p][/*][*][p]Enemies sometimes stopped acting mid-combat, breaking the flow of battle.[/p][/*][*][p]AI behavior was overly simple and predictable.[/p][/*][*][p]Some enemies would get stuck in walls or fail to navigate terrain properly.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Monsters will now calculate target distance instantly, rather than pausing before entering combat.[/p][/*][*][p]Aggro detection range will be increased.[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy attack behavior will adjust depending on the player’s distance.[/p][/*][*][p]Additional crowd control abilities will be added to diversify enemy patterns.[/p][/*][*][p]In accordance with the changes above, enemies will have clearer wind-up animations to ensure players can respond appropriately.[/p][/*][*][p]Monsters that get stuck in terrain will automatically reset their position.[/p][p] [/p][/*][/list][h2][b]10. Difficulty[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]PvE[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Players encountered sharp difficulty spikes when entering certain content too early.[/p][/*][*][p]Lack of guidance on recommended levels or clear progression paths caused players to give up.[/p][/*][*][p]The game’s non-linear design contributed to uneven difficulty jumps.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p][b]First Chrono Gate (Thousandfold Piercer)[/b][/p][list][*][p]Players will now reach the first Chrono Gate around level 5 instead of level 3.[/p][list][*][p]Additional progression paths will be introduced before entering the first Chrono Gate.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Players will have the option to enter the first Chrono Gate alongside an NPC for support.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Solo/Party Content[/b][/p][list][*][p]Solo and party content will have clearer rules and revised patterns.[/p][list][*][p]Solo content such as Chrono Gates, Labyrinths, and Trials will be redesigned with deeper, technical combat rather than fighting enemy mobs[/p][/*][*][p]Party content such as Expedition and Time Portals will feature varied mission objectives that emphasize strategic, role-based gameplay.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Others[/b][/p][list][*][p]Core content will now include guidance for recommended party size, level range, and gear score.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]B. [u]Combat UI & FX[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]UI elements such as notifications, buffs, and damage numbers frequently covered the screen.[/p][/*][*][p]Overly bright visual effects made it difficult to distinguish between ally and enemy skills.[/p][/*][*][p]Screen shake, excessive brightness, and overlapping effects hindered combat visibility.[/p][/*][*][p]Many skill effects appeared too similar and hard to distinguish.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]HUD will be redesigned to improve visibility of skill cooldowns and resource indicators.[/p][/*][*][p]Glow effects will be reduced, and combat visuals will be refined to ensure character motions are more visible.[/p][/*][*][p]Players will now have the option to toggle combat visuals.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2][b]11. PvP[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Duels[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]It was difficult to recognize duel zones due to the lack of clear visual boundaries.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]A visual barrier will be added to indicate the boundaries of the duel zone.[/p][/*][*][p]A warning notification will appear when a player nears the edge of the zone.[/p][/*][*][p]A result pop-up will be added at the end of each duel.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44935330/ab0b1d0eb5179ab2d1fb516073819bd31e9dc5ba.jpg"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][olist][*][p][b]World[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Region Structure[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Navigation[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Interactions[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Exploration Rewards[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Local Quests[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Dungeons[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Open World Content[/b]
[/p][/*][/olist][h2][b]1. World[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Content Density & Regional Distinction[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Low content density and a lack of regional distinction led to underutilized areas and reduced immersion.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]We’ll be increasing content density throughout the world and introducing new exploration elements, such as themed caves and diverse exploration routes.[/p][/*][*][p]To help players navigate through the world more easily, we’ll be adding landmarks to complex or hard-to-navigate areas.[/p][/*][*][p]Gathering materials such as herbs and ores will have clearer textures to make them easier to locate.[/p][/*][*][p]We’ll be adding scenic viewpoints that reveal breathtaking landscapes as players turn corners or reach elevated terrain.[/p][/*][*][p]Guidance elements will be added to travel paths to help players discover core content such as Chrono Gates.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3][b]B. [u]Bland & Repetitive Map Design[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Despite the expansive open world, terrain textures felt repetitive and underwhelming.[/p][/*][*][p]Environmental details lacked polish, creating a noticeable gap between what was shown in trailers.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Region-specific features such as swamps, misty forests, wildflower fields, and grasslands will be further enhanced to strengthen visual identity.[/p][/*][*][p]A dynamic grass system will be implemented, and the wind system will be improved to create immersive environmental interactions based on player movement.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2][b]2. Regional Structure[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Disjointed Regional Transitions & Unintuitive Pathing[/u][/b][/h3][p][b] [/b][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Players often got lost due to unintuitive pathing in certain regions.[/p][/*][*][p]Many players were unaware of the inn return feature and ended up running back to settlements.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Additional routes will be added to areas that require frequent backtracking.[/p][/*][*][p] The inn return feature will receive improved guidance and visibility.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]B. [u]World Map[/u][/b][/h3][p][b] [/b][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]The lack of terrain and altitude indicators made it difficult for players to navigate the world map.[/p][/*][*][p]The compass provided limited directional guidance, making it difficult for players to locate objectives even when nearby.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]The compass will now include altitude indicators, using up/down arrows to reflect the location of the objective.[/p][/*][*][p]Areas will be visually differentiated so that players can better identify points of interest.[/p][list][*][p]What is a Point of Interest (POI)?[/p][list][*][p]A POI is a visually distinct area—such as striking structures, lights, or objects—that catch players’ attention from a distance. These locations often lead to hidden rewards or special events.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Explored and unexplored content will be clearly marked on the World Map to help track exploration progress.[/p][/*][*][p]We’ll be enhancing the quest tracker to provide better guidance. However, for certain quests, guidance will only extend to a general area to encourage exploration.[/p][/*][*][p]Players will be able to place additional custom markers and use a new memo feature to track important locations or mark resource collection points.[/p][/*][*][p]Inconsistencies between terrain and the World Map will be corrected.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]C. [u]POI Exploration[/u][/b][/h3][p][b] [/b][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]POIs often lacked meaningful content or rewards, which led to a disappointing experience.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]We’ll be introducing hidden caves, narrative encounters, and gathering opportunities to POIs to make exploration more rewarding.[/p][/*][/list][h2]
[b]3. Navigation[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Traversable & Non-Traversable Terrains[/u][/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]It was difficult to distinguish climbable terrain due to a lack of visual cues.[/p][/*][*][p]Players often wasted time attempting to climb non-traversable terrain.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Non-traversable terrain will now feature distinct visual elements, such as rocks and cliffs at least twice the height of the player, to clearly indicate areas that cannot be climbed.[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h2][b]4. Interactions[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Gathering Feedback[/u][/b][/h3][p][b] [/b][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]It was difficult to tell if gathering was successful due to a lack of clear visual feedback.[/p][/*][*][p]Gathering effects were too plain, making the overall process tedious.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]Gathering animations, effects, and sounds will be enhanced to make the process more rewarding.[/p][/*][*][p]Visual and sound effects for material disappearance upon successful gathering will be enhanced.[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h3][b]B. [u]Interaction Improvements[/u][/b][/h3][p][b] [/b][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Interactive elements could only be triggered from specific positions, hindering gameplay experience.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]We’ll be enhancing interaction responsiveness and methods to deliver a more intuitive and immersive experience.[/p][list][*][p]All navigation data tied to interaction positioning will be thoroughly reviewed to ensure smoother and more accurate position alignment during interactions.[/p][/*][*][p]Interactive objects will now use short-press interactions, reducing unnecessary delays.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][b] [/b][/p][h2][b] 5. Exploration Rewards[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]A. [u]Reward Value[/u][/b][/h3][p][b] [/b][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]Exploration lacked meaningful ties to core content, which led to a weaker sense of purpose.[/p][/*][*][p]Rewards were not compelling enough, making exploration feel inefficient and less engaging.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]New Dynamic Quests and Chain Quests will be introduced, unlocked exclusively through exploring specific areas.[/p][/*][*][p]Hidden rewards will be added to strengthen the purpose of exploration.[/p][/*][*][p]Rare achievements and titles exclusive to exploration will be introduced.[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h3][b]B. [u]Content Engagement & Rewards[/u][/b][/h3][p][b] [/b][/p][p][b]\[Issues][/b][/p][list][*][p]The value of rewards often felt underwhelming compared to content difficulty, diminishing the intended loop of challenge, reward, and progression.[/p][/*][*][p]The drop rates of high-value items were too low, making content feel more tiring than motivating.[/p][/*][*][p]Progression was heavily reliant on life skills, which reduced the appeal of exploration, combat, and co-op activities, especially in early stages of the game.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]\[Our Plan][/b][/p][list][*][p]The progression structure will be refined to ensure players can progress through a variety of content, including world exploration.[/p][list][*][p]Each type of content will feature distinct progression mechanics designed to boost motivation and encourage participation.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][b] [/b][/p][h2][b] 6. Our goal is to deliver a story that allows players to become more deeply immersed in the world and its lore.[/b][/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]We are committed to improving [i]Chrono Odyssey[/i] through ongoing communication with our players. notes.title: Developer's Notes #2: End of the Closed Beta Part I
notes.content:
[p]Hello, this is the [i]Chrono Odyssey[/i] Development Team.[/p][p][/p][p]We want to thank everyone who joined the recent closed beta. Your support, curiosity, and genuine feedback have meant a lot to us. It’s been a privilege to watch players explore what we’ve built so far, and your input allows us to take an honest look at where the game stands and shape our next steps.[/p][p]We were excited to see that many of you enjoyed the core experience of [i]Chrono Odyssey[/i]. However, there are also areas that fell short. We heard consistent feedback on animations, motions, combat responsiveness, performance, optimization, graphics, etc. All forms of critique, whether big or small, are critical to the development process, and our top priority is to address these shortcomings accordingly.[/p][p]To that end, we’re carefully reviewing all the feedback you’ve shared. Some of it will be addressed here in Part 1, while the rest is being thoroughly reviewed and will be covered in detail in Part 2.[/p][list][*][p]Animation/Motion and Combat Experience Improvements (1/2)[/p][/*][*][p]Performance/Optimization[/p][/*][*][p]Lighting and Other Graphic Enhancements[/p][/*][/list][p]Here’s a look at some of the key areas we’re working to improve.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]1. Animations & Combat Responsiveness[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b][u]1) Hit Feedback Inconsistency[/u][/b][/h3][list][*][p]This was a major issue during the closed beta test. Some actions felt sluggish or disconnected, with attacks, dodges, and blocks occasionally failing to register as expected. We believe this stems from packet desyncs between the client and the server, and will accelerate packet transmission to [b]improve timing accuracy, redesign packet intervals, and refine the packet structure[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Currently, motion and combat packets are interconnected in a shared data stream, which may be contributing to sync issues. We plan on separating these into distinct systems, actively reviewing and resolving all collision detection inconsistencies to [b]ensure combat interactions feel consistent and responsive[/b].[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3] [b][u]2) Class Weapons[/u][/b][/h3][list][*][p]While each class has a wide range of abilities, we’ll be [b]introducing a new system called the “Matrix”[/b] in the next test to give each weapon a more distinct identity. This system will allow you to [b]choose from four progression paths per weapon [/b](twelve in total) as each class has three weapons.[/p][/*][*][p]We aim to [b]diversify skill usage of each weapon based on progression paths[/b]. Even if two players are using the same weapon, their primary skills may differ. The same skill can also produce different results depending on builds. Our goal is a [b]wide range of playstyles[/b], whether you're focusing on chaining skills, switching between weapons, or exploring other tactical options. Farming will become more dynamic, and players will need to find gear with stats that match their playstyle.[/p][/*][*][p]With added playstyles, we’re [b]creating new animations[/b] to ensure each weapon feels [b]distinct and expressive in combat[/b].[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3][b][u]3) Camera[/u][/b][/h3][list][*][p]We are fixing an issue where the [b]camera angle affects visibility[/b] when you’re too close to walls or certain environments.[/p][/*][*][p]The following issues with the lock-on system will also be addressed:[/p][list][*][p]Abrupt screen change when changing targets[/p][/*][*][p]Camera getting too close to the target during melee combat[/p][/*][*][p]Camera reset after combat[/p][/*][*][p]Skills being cast based on the direction the player is facing rather than the camera’s[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]We’re also addressing an issue where the [b]camera shakes vertically in certain areas.[/b][/p][/*][/list][h3][b][u]4) Controls[/u][/b][/h3][list][*][p]To enhance the overall feel of combat, we’re redesigning hit reactions by increasing the reaction duration from 1 to 2-4 seconds. This provides [b]clearer timing for follow-up attacks[/b] and adds a [b]greater sense of risk and reward[/b] when taking damage or landing hits.[/p][/*][*][p]We're also [b]reviewing and fixing unnatural character movements and collision inconsistencies[/b] that caused characters to appear as if floating.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2][b]2. Performance & Optimization[/b][/h2][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b][u]1) GPU & Rendering Overload[/u][/b][/h3][list][*][p]We’re restructuring how assets are rendered to[b] reduce GPU load and improve real-time performance[/b].[/p][list][*][p]High-resolution Nanite geometry will only be applied where necessary, while frequently repeated assets will rely on Instanced Static Mesh (ISM) or Hierarchical Instanced Static Mesh (HISM) to minimize draw calls and reduce GPU strain. Assets will be managed in batches, and draw calls will be consolidated to minimize CPU–GPU communication overhead and maximize rendering efficiency.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b][u]2) Development Efficiency[/u][/b][/h3][list][*][p]We're shifting level design toward reusable environmental assets to [b]improve development efficiency and runtime performance[/b] to speed up production and simplify maintenance, while reducing memory, disk, and rendering overhead.[/p][/*][*][p]We're also minimizing redundant materials and textures by standardizing our art pipeline with trim sheets, [b]ensuring high-resolution visual variety.[/b][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]▶[i] Trim sheets?[/i][/b][/h3][p][i]Trim sheets consolidate commonly used detail elements (such as metal edges, moldings, panel lines, and bolts) into a single texture laid out within a 0–1 UV space. Each asset is then UV-mapped to the appropriate section, allowing for a wide range of visual details using just one shared material. This eliminates the need to create separate high-resolution textures for every object. In Unreal Engine, trim sheet–based materials are loaded only once, which reduces memory usage and optimizes draw calls. By instancing parameters like color, roughness, and metallic values, we can easily introduce visual variety without adding performance cost. Trim sheets are particularly effective when applied to modular environment pieces and background structures that are frequently used throughout the game world.[/i][/p][p][/p][h3][b][u]3) Memory Usage[/u][/b][/h3][list][*][p]We're restructuring the loading system by separating rendering data from collision data to [b]reduce memory usage and improve system stability.[/b][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]▶[i] Collision data loaded alongside rendering data?[/i][/b][/h3][p][i]Previously, collision data was loaded alongside rendering data even when it wasn’t needed. With the new structure, only rendering data is loaded by default, while collision data is selectively loaded based on player proximity and line of sight, completely avoiding unnecessary memory usage. For Nanite meshes, we’re planning to replace per-polygon collision with simplified low-poly collision meshes to lower GPU and CPU overhead. Unused collision primitives will be unloaded from memory to further optimize resource usage and improve loading speed.[/i][/p][p][/p][list][*][p]We’ll be refining our Garbage Collection (GC) and memory allocation structure to [b]manage unused areas more efficiently.[/b][/p][list][*][p]Unused cells and actors within the World Partition system will be automatically unloaded, and the garbage collection timing will also be adjusted to remove unnecessary references more quickly.[/p][/*][*][p]Resources will be managed based on their data layer state with only active layers remain loaded, while assets in inactive layers are prevented from loading altogether. This ensures that only relevant assets consume memory, resulting in better performance and system stability.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b][u]4) Stable Performance Across Various System Specs[/u][/b][/h3][list][*][p]We’ll be designing a dynamic loading system that adjusts based on the player’s hardware: high-end systems for broader areas and higher-quality assets, lower-end systems for nearby cells and lower-resolution assets. This ensures a [b]balanced experience between performance and visual quality, regardless of system specs[/b].[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][h2][b]3. Graphics[/b][/h2][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b][u]1) Rendering Efficiency[/u][/b][/h3][list][*][p]We’ll be [b]reducing unnecessary calculations and streamlining the rendering pipeline[/b] without compromising visual quality.[/p][list][*][p]Redundant material shaders will be consolidated into unified master materials, managed entirely through instance parameters. [/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][/p][list][*][p]By improving ocean surface shaders and wave rendering, we aim to [b]enhance realism while minimizing GPU load[/b].[/p][list][*][p]To further optimize performance, we’ll be reducing reliance on World Position Offset (Vertex Animation), simplifying material functions, and replacing screen space reflections with a mix of cubemap reflections to achieve a better balance between visual quality and performance.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b][u]2) Screen Transition and Quality[/u][/b][/h3][list][*][p]We’re working to [b]improve overall screen quality[/b] by delivering high-resolution visuals and smoother transitions.[/p][list][*][p]By adjusting and migrating our Temporal Super Resolution (TSR) settings, we’ll be reducing motion blur and ghosting artifacts. [/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]▶[i] Temporal Super Resolution?[/i][/b][/h3][p][i]This update also enhances image clarity and frame stability compared to traditional Temporal Anti-Aliasing (TAA).[/i][/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Additionally, we’re adding support for DLSS (NVIDIA) and FSR (AMD) to [b]enhance both performance and visual quality.[/b][/p][list][*][p]Upscaling options will be available on compatible graphics cards to ensure players get the most out of their hardware.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b][u]3) Lighting[/u][/b][/h3][list][*][p]We’re working to [b]reduce unnecessary lighting calculations[/b] by removing unused lights and limiting the excessive use of Stationary and Movable lights.[/p][/*][*][p]We're also transitioning to a cluster-based light management system to reduce rendering costs, light overlap, and shading complexity, resulting in [b]more efficient rendering[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]To improve the overall quality of lighting, we’re standardizing exposure values and redefining the priority and range of key lights to improve[b] contrast fidelity and maintain consistent exposure[/b] across the scene.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]Please note that this update includes a number of technical terms. We’ve done our best to explain things clearly, and we appreciate your understanding as we focus on sharing our development plans as transparently as possible.[/p][p][/p][p]Part 2[b] [/b]will take a closer look at what’s ahead. In addition to the areas we’ve already covered, we’ll continue improving [b]combat systems, technical stability, graphics, and animations[/b]. We’ll also be addressing new topics such as [b]sound, UI/UX, gameplay flexibility, in-game guidance, balance, content flow, progression, replayability, social features, narrative, server stability, and bug fixes[/b].[/p][p]We don’t plan on rushing ahead without first getting things right. We want the next version of [i]Chrono Odyssey[/i] to reflect all the hard work and honest feedback that have gone into this process. Our focus remains on quality and delivering a more polished, complete experience.[/p][p][/p][p]Stay tuned for more details and as always, we look forward to hearing your feedback. Thank you again for being part of this journey.[/p][p][/p][p]- The [i]Chrono Odyssey[/i] Development Team[/p][p][/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Community Wrap-Up: Closed Beta
notes.content:
[p]Greetings Sentinels,
[/p][p]The curtains have closed on the first Chrono Odyssey Closed Beta.[/p][p]What began as a test quickly turned into something more meaningful, shaped by the passion and presence of our community. Whether you explored Setera on your own or joined forces to take down bosses, each and every one of you made a real impact.[/p][p][/p][p][b]We received an incredible range of feedback and reactions across Discord, X, and other channels🙏. All of it has been shared with the development team, and a more detailed update will be coming really soon through a Developer's Note.💕[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44935330/02dbbc66bcd15c595ea9e31ed9061a22daa5185b.png"][/img][/p][p]We've collected thousands of pieces of feedback across Discord, X, surveys, and more. [/p][p]Here are just a few highlights:[/p][p][/p][p][b]What you loved:[/b][/p][p]- The world of Setera is immersive and worth exploring.[/p][p]- The Chronotector system is unique and adds depth.[/p][p]- Character customization offers lots of options and creativity.[/p][p]- The game has solid core gameplay with strong potential. [/p][p][/p][p][b]What you want improved:[/b][/p][p]- Performance stability (FPS drops, visual stuttering) and optimization[/p][p]- Combat feedback and animation polish[/p][p]- Clearer quest objectives and map guidance[/p][p]- More intuitive UI and better PC controller support[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44935330/f6d9ebbe6b348464565c1fae5cd6fe29fa87a6b6.png"][/img][/p][p]We also had the pleasure of partnering with some amazing creators during this period. If you haven't already, check out their awesome takes on the game:[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="Wdzc1uUIBR4;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][previewyoutube="FbkwoaGmSwQ;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][previewyoutube="UsnjhcsLgmk;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h3]▶ [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2873440/view/532101750029549590"]Check out our Partners[/url][/h3][p][/p][p]We'll be continuing to support content creation through future stages of development, so stay tuned.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44935330/5e8623e0f4372c271bbd67e237eac1f67aeb4a92.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Character Creation, Chaos, and Memes[/b][/h3][p]You didn't just play the game, you made it your own. notes.title: Chrono Odyssey Closed Beta has ended
notes.content:
[p]Greetings Sentinels,
[/p][p]The first Closed Beta Test for Chrono Odyssey has officially concluded. We sincerely thank everyone who participated and expressed overwhelming interest far beyond our expectations.[/p][p]
During this brief testing period, we received a lot of feedback, bug reports, and thoughtful suggestions. We are carefully reviewing every submission, and your insights are playing a vital role in shaping the final quality of Chrono Odyssey.[/p][p]
At present, we are currently prioritizing improvements to key gameplay elements such as movement controls, animations and combat responsiveness. Our goal is to refine these systems to provide a more immersive and polished experience.
[/p][p]Performance and system stability issues are also undergoing in-depth review. We are committed to resolving these issues to ensure a more stable and more reliable gameplay experience.[/p][p][/p][p]In addition we are actively addressing bugs, optimization challenges and UI/UX-related inconveniences identified during the test, guided by the feedback provided during the closed beta.[/p][p][/p][p]If you haven't had the chance to complete the feedback survey, we would greatly appreciate it if you could take a moment to share your thoughts. Your input is invaluable in helping us make Chrono Odyssey better.[/p][p][/p][p][url="https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/CHRONOCBT" style="button"]Take the Survey[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Thank you once again for being part of this journey. We hope you'll continue to support us as we work towards delivering the best possible Chrono Odyssey experience.[/p]

notes.title: Time To Die In Chrono Odyssey’s Early Access Preview
notes.content:
I was genuinely interested to review Chrono Odyssey for one specific reason—it was the first MMORPG that I’ve played probably since World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King. Well, that’s not entirely true; I dabbled with New World back when it first came out, but adult life didn’t afford me much time to invest in it in earnest. So I was genuinely curious to see what MMOs were like nowadays, and I gotta say, things certainly have changed since I was a boy.

That’s mostly a joke, but there is a degree of truth to it. Back in the 2000s and early 2010s, so many MMOs desperately tried to replicate World of Warcraft’s success and subsequently faded into obscurity. Games like Guild Wars 2, City of Heroes, or even The Old Republic were a few of the standouts, but they all looked and played almost identically—that is to say, like World of Warcraft. 

Which is why Chrono Odyssey was so immediately striking to me because of just how different it felt from any of the MMOs I remembered... Read more

notes.title: Developer's Notes #1: What we've been up to
notes.content:
We want to express our heartfelt thanks to everyone who has been patiently waiting for our game. We know many of you have been eager to hear new updates, so today, we’d like to share a small part of what’s been going on.

[h3][b]Taking a Step Further[/b][/h3]
[hr][/hr][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44935330/65e041265d6dcb6ae626506b909f6f0d998a56b8.jpg[/img]
Back in February, we held a private [b]Focus Group Test[/b]. Many players participated and thanks to the amazing feedback and in-depth data, we’ve been able to further move forward with the direction of the game. Since then, we’ve been focusing on refining areas that needed improvement and pushing the overall polish to the next level. 

To give you a small glimpse of what was tested during the FGT, [b]Soroma Stronghold[/b] stood out as one of the most popular areas in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44935330/fa9174818a2ebf2a8ce60a9dcbde03b274b78e95.jpg[/img]
[i]There are rumors of a mysterious presence near Soroma Stronghold. To uncover the truth, someone may need to venture deep into the mist. [/i]

[i]Travelers will naturally come across this region during their journey, but Soroma Stronghold is far from just another exploration site.  It carries a strange, eerie atmosphere, as though something important is hidden within. What could be waiting inside?[/i]

Among all the content in the test, [b]Bounty Hunting[/b] came out as the most popular. Tracking and taking down powerful targets requires not just skill but a little bit of observation and patience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44935330/c3daf4c26e753e73736d64b3e2ef3a177e269667.png[/img]

[i]One of the most frequently hunted bounties was [b]Ravenous Bog[/b]. This hulking brute may appear clumsy, but don't let that fool you. As for where you might run into him… we’ll leave that for you to discover when the time comes.[/i]

[h3][b]Coming Soon[/b][/h3]
[hr][/hr]https://store.steampowered.com/app/2873440/Chrono_Odyssey/
Even at this very moment, our team is working to build and fine-tune every part of the game to bring you the best possible experience. And very soon, we believe the time will come when we can finally present Chrono Odyssey.

Your continued support and interest have been an incredible source of motivation for us. We’re doing our best to prepare so that we can share this world with everyone.

We’ll be back with even more exciting news next time.


Thank you,
[i]From the Chrono Odyssey Development Team. [/i]

notes.title: Letter from the Chrono Odyssey Producer
notes.content:
Hello, I'm Yun Sang Tae, the producer of Chrono Odyssey.

We are deeply grateful for your continued interest and support for Chrono Odyssey. Thank you for staying updated with our latest news and development progress.

Since the release of our latest trailer, the development team has been working relentlessly to deliver a game that truly meets the expectations of our players. The recent focus group test underscores our commitment to improving the game's combat experience, making it more engaging and immersive. We were relieved to find that most of the feedback from our testers was positive, and we are even more excited about the opportunity to present an enhanced Chrono Odyssey to all of you.

Chrono Odyssey is an "open-world MMORPG where time dictates destiny," and we are committed to integrating all the core elements showcased in the trailer into the game. Players will be able to experience exhilarating battles with colossal bosses, adventures that utilize the "Chronotector," a device that manipulates time and space, complex characters, and innovative storytelling. We look forward to the day we can share these features with you.

Our development team has dedicated countless hours to perfecting Chrono Odyssey. As a result, many parts of the game have been developed, and we are steadily approaching completion. Nonetheless, our commitment to refining Chrono Odyssey remains steadfast up to its final release. As an avid gamer myself, I understand the challenge of waiting for a game's release, but please bear with us a little longer!

We are dedicated to creating an exceptional title that meets the expectations of both our players and our development team. Your continued support is invaluable to us, and we are determined to meet your expectations. Together, we will embark on a journey to create an extraordinary Chrono Odyssey.

Thank you,
Yun Sang Tae

Follow us on our [url=https://x.com/ChronoOdyssey]official X [/url] to stay tuned for the latest updates on the Focus Group Testing and Chrono Odyssey. We will be posting updates regularly from now on!
